text:
maria: FYI pushed a prototype selector for CI perf-trace autocollect. wants to bias captures toward kernel hotspots + KV cold misses. please skim? :eyes:

sam: Nice. what's the sampling strategy? random or score-based?

maria: score-based. short summary: probabilistic sampler that combines recent kernel runtime heat, kv-miss rate, and run frequency. low overall rate so nightly job stays under storage cap. config snippet i used:

```
# selector config (yaml)
sampling:
  global_rate: 0.025   # 2.5% baseline
  score_weights:
    kernel_ms: 0.6
    kv_miss: 0.3
    infra_errors: 0.1
  max_per_nightly: 18
  min_per_model: 1
```

raj: Storage question: where do artifacts land and TTL? we need lifecycle hooks, otherwise s3 gets big. also encryption key.

maria: artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/nightly/$BUILD_ID/<selector>/; lifecycle 90d, archive to glacier after 30d, delete after 90d. KMS key = arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:...:key/pm-prod.

eric: For capture flags, use nsys to keep trace size bounded. prefer capture-range with NVTX markers in runtime. example command we run in CI agent:

```
nsys profile -o nightly/${BUILD_ID} --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --stats=true --output-format=sqlite,nsys
# then run: python tools/run_perf_smoke.py --warmup 3 --iter 5
```

sam: Also add a short perfetto CPU snapshot for kernel scheduling hotspots, e.g., `perfetto --config=...` or the CI agent collects `perf record -F 99 -a -g`. small compressed tar goes to s3.

maria: Good call. i'm limiting CPU dumps to first 3 candidates per-night to keep size small.

ci-bot: nightly-perf-job #2118 started by @maria. selector v1 applied. artifacts uploading to s3://redwood-perf/nightly/2118009876/ -> https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/nightly/2118009876 :white_check_mark:

raj: Can selector also prefer traces where kernel selection changed between baseline and candidate? e.g., if kernel X->X_int8 happened, that's high-value.

maria: yes that's in plan: diff hints from last-good run feed the heuristic. we score +2 for kernel-switch.

eric: quick nit: ensure CI agent strips PII and model weights, only kernel timelines + nvtx ranges + minimal input hash. Security wants that.

maria: agreed — added sanitizer step in upload: `tools/sanitize_trace.py --redact-inputs --strip-weights`.

sam: Once we have nightly artifacts, can we auto-generate perf diffs and flag regressions over thresholds? i can wire up a small lambda to run `perf-diff` and push alerts to #incidents if >5% tail-latency regress.

maria: that's the goal. linking to new diff dashboard MVP: https://perf.redwood.internal/diff/compare?base=last-good&run=2118009876 - shows kernel timeline overlays + KV miss heatmap.

raj: one more: can we randomize a tiny portion of samples across regions to catch infra-specific regressions?

maria: yes — selector already supports region shard weights. default 10% multi-region.

sam: looks good to me. can we get a quick end-to-end run tomorrow and a small postmortem if anything noisy shows up? :rocket:

maria: will run E2E tomorrow, capture sample list and upload to dashboard. please ack if you want to be on the review list.

eric: ack

raj: ack

sam: ack :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will follow up with PR & CI job link.
